content: 1. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gastrointestinal tract. However, systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor when co-administering. 2. Omeprazole and cyclosporine may increase each other's toxicity through mechanisms not fully understood. Use caution and monitor closely. Long-term use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) may cause hypomagnesemia, which can increase the risk of magnesium depletion when combined with other drugs that also lower magnesium levels. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration of dabigatran with P-glycoprotein inhibitors in patients with atrial fibrillation if creatinine clearance (CrCl) is less than 30 mL/min. For deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment, avoid co-administration if CrCl is less than 50 mL/min. 5. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Use alternative therapies if available. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to oral forms of both agents. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal tract pH (e.g., PPIs, H2-blockers, antacids) may reduce dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. 6. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dapsone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Omeprazole and dextroamphetamine interaction may alter pharmacokinetics. Reduced gastric acidity caused by PPIs decreases the time to maximum concentration (Tmax) for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine, though the area under the curve (AUC) remains unaffected. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of darolutamide by mechanisms involving P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4. Darolutamide is a substrate of both P-gp and CYP3A4. Monitor for increased adverse reactions and adjust the darolutamide dose as needed when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Consider alternative antibiotics if clarithromycin is co-administered with darunavir (plus ritonavir or cobicistat). Darunavir increases clarithromycin levels by decreasing its metabolism. No dose adjustment is necessary in normal renal function, but reduce the clarithromycin dose by 50% if CrCl is 30–60 mL/min and by 75% if CrCl is less than 30 mL/min. 11. Clarithromycin and dasatinib both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of daunorubicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of deflazacort by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 15. Clarithromycin and deutetrabenazine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. However, certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation) may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of diazepam (buccal or intranasal) by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases diazepam levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Dichlorphenamide and omeprazole both decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It may also decrease their levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but an alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Omeprazole increases digoxin toxicity through other mechanisms. Prolonged PPI use may cause hypomagnesemia, increasing the risk of digoxin toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Efavirenz increases omeprazole levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Clarithromycin and dolasetron both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of donepezil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of doravirine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of doxepin cream by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin (including liposomal formulations) by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib AUC, which may increase the risk of duvelisib toxicities. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Elagolix increases omeprazole levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. No dose adjustments are needed for omeprazole at doses of 40 mg/day or less. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 35. Clarithromycin increases elagolix levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 36. Elagolix decreases omeprazole levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 37. Omeprazole increases eluxadoline levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, use caution when co-administered with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Clarithromycin increases elvitegravir levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase its levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Clarithromycin and erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate forms) increase each other's levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Eslcarbazepine acetate increases omeprazole levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Clarithromycin decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Clarithromycin increases estradiol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Clarithromycin increases estradiol vaginal levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of estrogens. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Clarithromycin decreases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clarithromycin increases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Clarithromycin increases esterified estrogens levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Clarithromycin decreases estropipate levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Clarithromycin increases estropipate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Clarithromycin increases eszopiclone levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption and by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely.
